feedback: Judged before racing. The candidate is valid and is the iteration 8 design (best raced at 116.27, sensors x -0.03..0.03 at y 0.06, sensor_size 0.012) with one change: controller.kp from 4.0 to 3.7. The rationale rests on iteration 8's oval steering_oscillation of 0.262, which is above the 0.25 concern level. Across iterations 1 to 4 at fixed kd, raising kp raised oscillation (kp 3.0 at kd 0.15 gave 0.164 on the oval; kp 4.0 at kd 0.20 gave 0.208), so a modest kp reduction is supported. The change is a single-variable step of 0.3, and kd, ki, base_speed and line_loss are unchanged. The risk is that lower kp reduces progress on bends. Iteration 8 progress was 0.46 on the oval, 0.26 on the s-bend and 0.12 on the slalom, so progress is the number to watch. Nothing about this candidate's outcome has been measured. max_error has stayed at 0.061 to 0.065 m in every iteration 0 to 8, so this change is unlikely to remove the off-track floor. It is aimed at oscillation and should be judged mainly on steering_oscillation and progress. Once the race reports, decide as follows. If the score is at or above 116.27 with oval oscillation under 0.25, keep kp 3.7 as the base. If the score falls below 116.27 with oscillation under 0.25, restore kp 4.0 and test a narrower spread (x -0.02..0.02) at kd 0.30, as the Optimizer's own fallback plan says. If oscillation stays above 0.25 at kp 3.7, lower kd is not the answer (iteration 3 to 4 showed kd up raising oscillation); test kp 3.4 instead. Do not raise base_speed above 1.3 until progress nears 0.995 with no line loss, since every run so far has gone off track.
requested_changes: If the score falls below 116.27 with oval steering_oscillation under 0.25, restore controller.kp to 4.0 and test geometry.sensor_positions x at -0.02..0.02 (y 0.06, sensor_size 0.012, kd 0.30). Iteration 8 showed that the narrower spread raised progress, so a further narrowing is the next lever, not a gain change.

If oval steering_oscillation stays above 0.25 at kp 3.7, lower controller.kp further to about 3.4 with kd 0.30 unchanged. Iteration 4 (kd 0.25) and iteration 3 (kd 0.20) show that raising kd did not reduce oscillation, so kp is the lever to move.
Keep controller.base_speed at 1.3 and do not raise it until progress nears 0.995 with no line loss. Iterations 0 to 8 all went off track, so speed matters only once the robot stays on the line.
